LECTURE 3Nervous System Overview

Lecturer: Dr Nur Hassan, BDS, PGT (Oral Surg), PhD — Head of Department, Head & Neck Anatomy.

Central nervous system (CNS)

  • Brain
  • Spinal cord

Peripheral nervous system (PNS)

  • Cranial nerves — 12 pairs
  • Spinal nerves — 31 pairs

MENINGESMeninges & Dural Spaces

The three layers (outer → inner)

  • Dura mater — thick, tough; outer layer
  • Arachnoid mater — delicate; intermediate layer; spans the contours of the brain
  • Pia mater — inner layer; firmly attached to and follows the contours of the brain

Dural spaces

  • Extradural (epidural) space — potential space
  • Subdural space — potential space
  • Subarachnoid space — the only true space, filled with CSF

Meningeal haemorrhages (clinical)

BleedLocationSource
Epidural (extradural) haematomaBetween skull & duraRuptured middle meningeal artery
Subdural haematomaBetween dura & arachnoidTorn bridging veins (to superior sagittal sinus)
Subarachnoid haemorrhageSubarachnoid spaceRuptured aneurysm

Dural folds (reflections)

  • Falx cerebri — between the 2 cerebral hemispheres
  • Falx cerebelli — between the 2 cerebellar hemispheres
  • Tentorium cerebelli — between cerebellum and cerebrum; roofs the posterior cranial fossa
  • Diaphragma sellae — roof of the sella turcica (sphenoid); has a circular hole for the pituitary stalk (infundibulum)

VENOUSDural Venous Sinuses

Sinuses (tap to reveal in quiz mode)
Superior sagittal sinusInferior sagittal sinus Straight sinusConfluence of sinuses Transverse sinusSigmoid sinus Superior petrosal sinusInferior petrosal sinus Cavernous sinusIntercavernous sinus Sphenoparietal sinusBasilar sinus Great cerebral veinOphthalmic vein

Cavernous sinus

  • Large venous plexus on each side of the sella turcica.
  • In the lateral wall: CN III, CN IV, V1, V2.
  • Passing through the sinus: CN VI and the internal carotid artery (ICA).
  • Clinical: cavernous sinus thrombosis — can follow spread of infection from the paranasal/central face; may compress the nerves within.
Exam tip: the abducent nerve (VI) runs through the sinus (not in the wall), so it is the nerve most likely affected first in cavernous sinus thrombosis → lateral rectus palsy.

BRAINDivisions of the Brain

  • Cerebrum
  • Cerebellum
  • Brainstem = midbrain + pons + medulla

Cerebrum

  • Site of memory, intelligence and personality.
  • 2 hemispheres divided by the longitudinal fissure, joined by the corpus callosum.
  • Surface features: elevations = gyri; grooves = sulci; deeper grooves = fissures.

Cerebral hemispheres — lobes & functions

LobeMain functions
FrontalMovement / speech (motor), reasoning, emotions, personality, problem solving
ParietalSensory (pain, pressure, temperature, touch); spatial orientation; comprehension of language
TemporalAuditory perception, learning & memory
OccipitalVision
InsulaVisceral functions; taste

Median sagittal section — diencephalon & pituitary

  • Corpus callosum.
  • Thalamus — relays sensory & motor signals to the cortex; regulates consciousness, sleep, alertness.
  • Hypothalamus — controls the autonomic nervous system & endocrine system.
  • Pituitary — produces hormones: GH, ACTH, FSH, prolactin, TSH, ADH, oxytocin.

Cerebellum

Functions in motor control and motor learning.

Brainstem

  • Midbrain — cerebral peduncles.
  • Pons.
  • Medulla — pyramids (motor function) and olives (control & coordination of movement; aid perception of sound).

CORDSpinal Cord

  • Begins at the caudal end of the medulla; ends at L1–L2 in a tapering conus medullaris.
  • Filum terminale — fibrous thread anchoring the cord below the conus.
  • Cauda equina — the bundle of lumbosacral nerve roots below the conus.
  • 31 pairs of spinal nerves.
Slide correction: the roots are dorsal root = sensory (afferent) and ventral root = motor (efferent). (The lecture slide labelled both “motor” — that is a typo.)

CSFCSF Spaces & Ventricles

  • CSF sits in the subarachnoid space.
  • CSF is produced by the choroid plexus of the ventricles.
  • CSF is drained into the venous sinuses through the arachnoid granulations.

Flow of CSF through the ventricular system

  • 2 lateral ventricles → via the interventricular foramen (of Monro)
  • → 3rd ventricle → via the cerebral aqueduct
  • → 4th ventricle → via the median & lateral apertures → subarachnoid space

Hydrocephalus

  • Excess CSF.
  • Caused by partial obstruction of the flow of CSF.

BLOODBlood Supply of the Brain

Internal carotid artery (ICA)

PartLocation / note
1 · Cervical partNo branches
2 · Petrous partIn the carotid canal
3 · Cavernous partIn the cavernous sinus
4 · Cerebral partIntra-dural part

Supplies the brain and forms part of the circle of Willis.

Circle of Willis

ICA → supply the cerebrum

  • Anterior cerebral artery (joined by the anterior communicating artery)
  • Middle cerebral artery

Vertebral → basilar → supply cord, brainstem, cerebellum

  • Vertebral arteries → basilar artery
  • Posterior cerebral artery (joined by the posterior communicating artery)

PNSPeripheral Nervous System

Cranial nerves

12 pairs

Spinal nerves — 31 pairs

  • Cervical – 8
  • Thoracic – 12
  • Lumbar – 5
  • Sacral – 5
  • Coccygeal – 1
